l: Japji, Japji, Japji .. 36 In the realm of knowledge the light of divine knowledge is resplendent. There are heard songs from which millions of joys and pleasures proceed. Beauty is the attribute of the realm of happiness. There things are fashioned in an incomparable manner. What is done there cannot be described. Whoever endeavoureth to describe it shall afterwards repent. There are fashioned knowledge, wisdom, intellect, and understanding; And there too is fashioned the skill of demigods and men of supernatural power.
s: This unit concerns God, the True One, and how people know, praise, hear, and obey Him. It describes God's order, gifts, creation, judgment, and the limits of human power to describe Him. It explains the benefits of hearing God's Name, obeying God, receiving the Guru's instruction, and attaining divine knowledge, virtue, and salvation. It also describes the realm of righteousness, the realm of knowledge, and the realm of happiness.

There dwell congregations of saints They rejoice; the True One is in their hearts. God dwelleth in the true realm. He looketh on its denizens with an eye of favour, and rendereth them happy. There are continents, worlds, and universes. Whoever trieth to describe them shall never arrive at an end. There are worlds upon worlds and forms upon forms. They fulfil their functions according to God's orders: God beholding and contemplating them is pleased. Nanak, to describe them would be impossible. .. Slok / The air is the guru, water our father, and the great earth our mother; Day and night are our two nurses, male and
s: The unit describes the realm of action, whose inhabitants include powerful warriors, heroes, and many Sitas, and whose force is incomparable. It describes congregations of saints who rejoice with the True One in their hearts and the true realm where God dwells. It explains that God favors its inhabitants and is pleased while beholding the continents, worlds, universes, and their forms. Nanak teaches that divine practice involves melting God's name in divine love, and that those who ponder on the Name may be emancipated.

l: So Dar and So Purukh (the Rahiras), So Dar and So Purukh (the Rahiras), Sodar
s: Sodar presents hymns by Guru Nanak, Guru Ram Das, and Guru Arjan concerning God, His greatness, His Name, creation, and devotion. Guru Nanak describes all beings and worlds singing God’s praises and says that God is eternal, sovereign, and beyond description. The hymns teach that remembering the true Name gives life and satisfaction, while forgetting it brings spiritual loss. Guru Ram Das and Guru Arjan emphasize the protection of the true Guru, the company of the saints, and God’s provision for all creatures.

l: Sodar, So Dar and So Purukh (the Rahiras), Sodar
s: Sodar contains hymns concerning God’s greatness, His Name, creation, devotion, and the company of the saints.

l: Guru Nanak, So Dar and So Purukh (the Rahiras), Sodar
s: Guru Nanak describes all creation as singing God’s praises and says that God is eternal, true, sovereign, and beyond complete description. He teaches that remembering the true Name gives life, while forgetting it leaves people spiritually empty.

l: God, So Dar and So Purukh (the Rahiras), Sodar
s: God is described as eternal, true, sovereign, and the creator and sustainer of the world, the continents, the worlds, and the universe. God provides daily food for all creatures, gives grace, and does what pleases Himself.

l: the true Lord, So Dar and So Purukh (the Rahiras), Sodar
s: The true Lord is identified with the eternal and true God whose greatness cannot be fully described and whose Name is true.

l: God's name, So Dar and So Purukh (the Rahiras), Sodar
s: The true Name is difficult to repeat but brings life and removes pain when remembered and cherished. Forgetting it leaves people spiritually without worth.

l: the universe, So Dar and So Purukh (the Rahiras), Sodar
s: The universe is made and supported by God’s hands and is among the many things that sing His praises.

l: saints, So Dar and So Purukh (the Rahiras), Sodar
s: Saints who please God and are imbued with His love sing His praises. Those who meet the saints are saved and come to know God’s attributes.

l: Guru Ram Das, So Dar and So Purukh (the Rahiras), Sodar
s: Guru Ram Das urges servants of God and the true Guru to supplicate Him and seek enlightenment with God’s Name. He teaches that the company of the saints reveals God’s attributes and brings the relish of His Name.

l: the true Guru, So Dar and So Purukh (the Rahiras), Sodar
s: The true Guru protects seekers and mercifully enlightens them with God’s Name. Those who enter the true Guru’s protection and society are blessed, while those who do not are described as unfortunate.

l: the company of the saints, So Dar and So Purukh (the Rahiras), Sodar
s: The company of the saints brings salvation, reveals God’s attributes, and gives people the relish of God’s Name. Meeting this company is described as a blessing.

l: Guru Arjan, So Dar and So Purukh (the Rahiras), Sodar
s: Guru Arjan teaches that God provides food for every creature and that people need not fear for their daily sustenance. He says that the society of the saints saves people and, through the Guru’s favour, raises and renews them.

l: God's praises, So Dar and So Purukh (the Rahiras), Sodar
s: God’s praises are sung by wind, water, fire, divine beings, holy men, heroes, singers, creatures, and the worlds. His praises are beyond complete enumeration or description.

l: So Dar and So Purukh (the Rahiras), So Dar and So Purukh (the Rahiras), So Purukh
s: This unit concerns God as the pure, infinite, and supreme Creator who pervades every heart, sustains all creatures, and determines what comes to pass. Guru Ram Das teaches that those who meditate on God, serve Him, and receive His kindness gain happiness, freedom from fear, and absorption in God's name. Guru Nanak confesses human weakness and warns that worldly love causes humanity to drown in forgetfulness and misery. Guru Arjan urges humanity to use the human body to meet God, join the saints, repeat God's name, and prepare to cross the terrible ocean.

l: Guru Ram Das, So Dar and So Purukh (the Rahiras), So Purukh
s: Guru Ram Das praises God as the true Creator, the giver and enjoyer, and the one Supreme Being contained in every heart. He teaches that those who meditate on and serve God become happy, emancipated, fearless, and absorbed in Him. He also teaches that only those saints who please God are truly good saints.

l: Guru Nanak, So Dar and So Purukh (the Rahiras), So Purukh
s: Guru Nanak calls himself helpless, impure, untrue, unlearned, and foolish, and says that he has sought the shelter of those who do not forget God. He praises God as the eternal Creator and declares that what God pleases and does comes to pass. He says that under the Guru's instruction God becomes manifest.

l: Guru Arjan, So Dar and So Purukh (the Rahiras), So Purukh
s: Guru Arjan teaches that obtaining a human body is an opportunity to meet God. He urges humanity to join the saints, repeat God's name, and prepare to cross the terrible ocean. He confesses that his actions have been base and asks God to preserve his honour.

l: God, So Dar and So Purukh (the Rahiras), So Purukh
s: God is described as pure, inaccessible, illimitable, infinite, fearless, omnipotent, and the eternal Creator. God provides for all creatures, gives the jewel of God's name to those shown kindness, separates some and blends others with Himself, and knows all creation. Those who meditate on, worship, and serve God gain happiness, emancipation, freedom from fear, and absorption in Him.

l: holy men, So Dar and So Purukh (the Rahiras), So Purukh
s: Saints are urged to meditate on God, and those who do so abide in happiness and are emancipated from Death's noose. Many saints praise God through varied worship, austerities, repetition of God's name, study, and religious duties. The truly good saints are those who please God.

l: humanity, So Dar and So Purukh (the Rahiras), So Purukh
s: Humanity is portrayed as helpless, forgetful, spiritually weak, and prone to drowning in worldly love. Human beings receive different roles as givers and beggars within God's wondrous play. Guru Arjan teaches that humanity should use the human body to meet God, join the saints, repeat God's name, and prepare for the crossing.

l: God's name, So Dar and So Purukh (the Rahiras), So Purukh
s: Those shown kindness by God obtain the jewel of God's name. Serving God brings happiness and absorption in God's name, while repeating God's name is presented as necessary preparation for crossing the terrible ocean.

l: creation, So Dar and So Purukh (the Rahiras), So Purukh
s: God fashioned the whole creation, and everything made belongs to God. Creation is described as God's play, with all living creatures contained in God, though what has been created will eventually disappear.

l: worldly love, So Dar and So Purukh (the Rahiras), So Purukh
s: Worldly love causes humanity's life to pass vainly and prevents humanity from moving through the mire in which it is drowning. Forgetfulness associated with worldly love causes virtues to melt away and keeps humanity from thinking of God.

l: Sohila (Kirtan Sohila), Sohila (Kirtan Sohila), Guru Nanak, Rag Gauri Dipaki
s: Guru Nanak's Rag Gauri Dipaki describes singing the Sohila in a house where God's praise is sung and He is meditated on. It praises the Fearless Lord and the Creator, whose gifts and care cannot be fully appraised. The speaker, described as a bride, awaits meeting her Lord while relations prepare for her marriage. The passage urges remembrance of the Caller because the day is approaching.

l: Guru Nanak, Sohila (Kirtan Sohila), Guru Nanak, Rag Gauri Dipaki
s: Guru Nanak teaches remembrance of the Caller and says that the approaching day should be remembered.

l: Rag Gauri Dipaki, Sohila (Kirtan Sohila), Guru Nanak, Rag Gauri Dipaki
s: Rag Gauri Dipaki presents teachings about singing the Sohila, praising God, and awaiting the Lord. It describes marriage preparations and urges remembrance of the approaching day.

l: God, Sohila (Kirtan Sohila), Guru Nanak, Rag Gauri Dipaki
s: God is praised and meditated on in the house. He is described as the Giver whose gifts cannot be appraised and who watches over living things and regards their wants.

l: Sohila, Sohila (Kirtan Sohila), Guru Nanak, Rag Gauri Dipaki
s: The Sohila is sung in the house where God's praise is sung and He is meditated on. It is called a song of joy through which everlasting comfort is obtained.

l: speaker (the bride), Sohila (Kirtan Sohila), Guru Nanak, Rag Gauri Dipaki
s: The speaker is a bride whose marriage year and auspicious time have been recorded. Relations meet and pour oil on her, and she asks her friends to pray that she may meet her Lord.

l: Sohila (Kirtan Sohila), Sohila (Kirtan Sohila), Guru Nanak, Rag Asa
s: Guru Nanak teaches that there are six schools of philosophy, six teachers, and six doctrines, but the Guru of gurus is one despite having various forms. He urges preservation of the system in which the Creator is praised. He explains that, like one sun across many seasons and divisions of time, there is one God although His forms are many.

l: Guru Nanak, Sohila (Kirtan Sohila), Guru Nanak, Rag Asa
s: Guru Nanak teaches that there is one God, although His forms are many.

l: six schools of philosophy, Sohila (Kirtan Sohila), Guru Nanak, Rag Asa
s: The six schools of philosophy are described as having six teachers and six doctrines.

l: God, Sohila (Kirtan Sohila), Guru Nanak, Rag Asa
s: God is one, although His forms are many.

l: system in which the Creator is praised, Sohila (Kirtan Sohila), Guru Nanak, Rag Asa
s: The system in which the Creator is praised should be preserved, and doing so will redound to the father's glory.

l: Sohila (Kirtan Sohila), Sohila (Kirtan Sohila), Guru Nanak, Rag Dhanasari
s: Guru Nanak presents a vision of worship addressed to God, in which the sun, moon, stars, wind, forests, and sandal perfume form a cosmic offering. God is described as having countless eyes, forms, feet, and organs of smell, yet no single one of each. The light in everything is identified as God's light, made manifest through the Guru's teaching. Guru Nanak longs for God's lotus feet and asks for divine favour so he may dwell in God's name.

l: Guru Nanak, Sohila (Kirtan Sohila), Guru Nanak, Rag Dhanasari
s: Guru Nanak describes the cosmic worship offered to God and recognizes God's light in everything. He compares his longing for God's lotus feet to a bumble-bee's attraction to a flower and asks for God's favour so he may dwell in God's name.

l: God, Sohila (Kirtan Sohila), Guru Nanak, Rag Dhanasari
s: God is addressed as the Lord of light and the Destroyer of birth. God's worship is formed by the sun, moon, stars, sandal perfume, wind, forests, and ecstatic strains, while God is described as having a thousand forms and organs yet no single form or organ.

l: worship, Sohila (Kirtan Sohila), Guru Nanak, Rag Dhanasari
s: Worship consists of the cosmos itself: the sun and moon are lamps, the firmament is a salver, the stars are pearls, sandal perfume is incense, the wind is a fan, and the forests are flowers. What pleases God is identified as real worship.

l: light, Sohila (Kirtan Sohila), Guru Nanak, Rag Dhanasari
s: The light in everything is God's light, and everything is brilliant because of it. The Guru's teaching makes this light manifest.

l: Sohila (Kirtan Sohila), Sohila (Kirtan Sohila), Guru Ram Das, Rag Gauri Purbi
s: Guru Ram Das teaches that lust and wrath are destroyed through meeting the saints, who are found by predestination and absorbed in God’s love. He praises saluting and prostrating before saints, while warning that pride causes pain and death. The saints of God are absorbed in God’s Name and have overcome the fear and pain of transmigration. The speaker asks God for preservation and declares that the Name is Nanak’s support and brings happiness.

l: Guru Ram Das, Sohila (Kirtan Sohila), Guru Ram Das, Rag Gauri Purbi
s: Guru Ram Das teaches that meeting the saints destroys lust and wrath. He praises reverence toward the saints and warns against the suffering caused by pride.

l: God, Sohila (Kirtan Sohila), Guru Ram Das, Rag Gauri Purbi
s: God is described as the imperishable Being whose love absorbs the soul. The speaker asks God, the greatest of the great, to preserve the poor and wretched.

l: the saints of God, Sohila (Kirtan Sohila), Guru Ram Das, Rag Gauri Purbi
s: The saints of God are absorbed in God’s Name and have destroyed the pain and fear of transmigration. They have found God the imperishable Being and possess great honour throughout the earth and universe.

l: transmigration, Sohila (Kirtan Sohila), Guru Ram Das, Rag Gauri Purbi
s: The saints of God have destroyed the pain and fear associated with transmigration.

l: God's name, Sohila (Kirtan Sohila), Guru Ram Das, Rag Gauri Purbi
s: The Name is Nanak’s support and prop. The speaker says happiness was obtained through being absorbed only in God’s Name.

l: Sohila (Kirtan Sohila), Sohila (Kirtan Sohila), Guru Arjan, Rag Gauri Purbi
s: Guru Arjan teaches that people should serve the saints and earn the profit of God's name. He says human life grows shorter, urges people to meet the Guru and arrange their affairs, and contrasts this world’s wickedness and superstition with salvation through knowing God. Those awakened by God and given the essence of His word can understand the Ineffable, find peace in God's palace, and avoid returning to this world. Nanak prays to become the dust of the saints' feet and receive happiness.

l: Guru Arjan, Sohila (Kirtan Sohila), Guru Arjan, Rag Gauri Purbi
s: Guru Arjan urges people to serve the saints, earn God's name, meet the Guru, and arrange their affairs. He teaches that by the Guru's favour God will dwell in the heart.

l: God, Sohila (Kirtan Sohila), Guru Arjan, Rag Gauri Purbi
s: God awakens people and causes them to drink the essence of His word, enabling them to know the story of the Ineffable. God may dwell in the heart by the Guru's favour and grants a home in His palace.

l: Guru Nanak, Sohila (Kirtan Sohila), Guru Arjan, Rag Gauri Purbi
s: Nanak calls himself the slave and craves the happiness of being made the dust of the saints' feet.

l: the saints of God, Sohila (Kirtan Sohila), Guru Arjan, Rag Gauri Purbi
s: The saints are to be served, and becoming the dust of their feet is presented as a source of happiness.

l: human life, Sohila (Kirtan Sohila), Guru Arjan, Rag Gauri Purbi
s: Human life grows shorter every day and night, so people are urged to meet the Guru and arrange their affairs.

l: this world, Sohila (Kirtan Sohila), Guru Arjan, Rag Gauri Purbi
s: This world is involved in wickedness and superstition. Those who know God are saved from it.

l: the next world, Sohila (Kirtan Sohila), Guru Arjan, Rag Gauri Purbi
s: The next world is described as a place where those who earn God's name will abide in happiness.

l: God's name, Sohila (Kirtan Sohila), Guru Arjan, Rag Gauri Purbi
s: God's name is described as a profit that people should earn in this life.

l: happiness, Sohila (Kirtan Sohila), Guru Arjan, Rag Gauri Purbi
s: Happiness is promised in the next world and in God's palace, and Nanak craves it through becoming the dust of the saints' feet.

l: Asa ki War (Asa di Var), Asa ki War (Asa di Var), Asa ki War (Asa di Var)
s: Asa ki War (Asa di Var) is presented in a translation by Max Arthur Macauliffe in The Sikh Religion, volume 1, published in 1909. The unit states that one God is true-named, the Creator, fearless, without enmity, immortal, unborn, self-existent, great, and beneficent. Guru Har Gobind is named. The War includes sloks attributed to the first Guru, which are to be sung to the air of “Tunda As Raja.”

l: Asa ki War (Asa di Var), Asa ki War (Asa di Var), Asa ki War (Asa di Var)
s: Asa ki War (Asa di Var) is presented as translated by Max Arthur Macauliffe in The Sikh Religion, volume 1, published in 1909. It includes sloks.

l: God, Asa ki War (Asa di Var), Asa ki War (Asa di Var)
s: One God is described as having a true name and as the Creator. The unit describes this God as devoid of fear and enmity, immortal, unborn, self-existent, great, and beneficent.

l: Guru Har Gobind, Asa ki War (Asa di Var), Asa ki War (Asa di Var)
s: Guru Har Gobind is named in the unit.

l: sloks, Asa ki War (Asa di Var), Asa ki War (Asa di Var)
s: The sloks in Asa ki War are stated to have been written by the first Guru. They are to be sung to the air of “Tunda As Raja.”

l: Asa ki War (Asa di Var), Asa ki War (Asa di Var), Slok .. Pauri I
s: The unit praises the Guru and describes the darkness that remains without him, even under immense light. Guru Nanak is praised as a teacher who makes demigods out of men and warns that clever people who disregard the Guru will be abandoned like spurious sesames. Guru Angad teaches that a hundred moons and a thousand suns cannot dispel the darkness without the Guru. Pauri I describes God as the Creator who made the world, gave names to things, created Maya, and gives and takes life.

l: Guru Nanak, Asa ki War (Asa di Var), Slok .. Pauri I
s: Guru Nanak is praised as one who, through the Guru, makes demigods out of men. He warns that those who consider themselves clever but do not think of the Guru will be abandoned like spurious sesames, bearing fruit and flower but containing ashes within.

l: Guru Angad, Asa ki War (Asa di Var), Slok .. Pauri I
s: Guru Angad teaches that even a hundred moons and a thousand suns would leave appalling darkness without the Guru.

l: True Guru, Asa ki War (Asa di Var), Slok .. Pauri I
s: The Guru is presented as necessary to dispel spiritual darkness, which remains even amid the light of a hundred moons and a thousand suns.

l: God, Asa ki War (Asa di Var), Slok .. Pauri I
s: God Himself created the world and gave names to things. God created Maya by His power, knows all things, and gives and takes life with a word.

l: world, Asa ki War (Asa di Var), Slok .. Pauri I
s: The world was created by God, who Himself gave names to things within it.

l: Maya, Asa ki War (Asa di Var), Slok .. Pauri I
s: Maya was created by God through His power.

l: Asa ki War (Asa di Var), Asa ki War (Asa di Var), Slok II .. Pauri II
s: Guru Nanak declares that God's regions, universes, worlds, creation, acts, thoughts, order, court, command, favour, signs, power, strength, praises, eulogies, and might are true. Guru Nanak teaches that those who meditate on the True One are true, while those who are born and die are the falsest of the false. Guru Angad describes the world as the True One's chamber and dwelling, where God acts according to His order and reveals Himself to those who become holy. Pauri II states that God created animals, recorded their names, appointed Dharmraj to judge their acts, and separates the truthful from those attached to mammon.

l: Guru Nanak, Asa ki War (Asa di Var), Slok II .. Pauri II
s: Guru Nanak declares God's regions, universes, worlds, creation, acts, thoughts, order, court, command, favour, signs, power, strength, praises, eulogies, and might to be true. He teaches that those who meditate on the True One are true, while those who are born and die are the falsest of the false.

l: Guru Angad, Asa ki War (Asa di Var), Slok II .. Pauri II
s: Guru Angad teaches that the world is the True One's chamber and dwelling. He says that God acts according to His order, withdraws some from mammon, leaves others in it, and reveals Himself to those known as holy.

l: God, Asa ki War (Asa di Var), Slok II .. Pauri II
s: God is described as true in His regions, universes, worlds, creation, acts, thoughts, order, court, command, behest, favour, signs, power, strength, praises, eulogies, and might. God gives without consulting others, is all in all Himself, acts by His own will, created animals, recorded their names, appointed Dharmraj, and judges and separates beings.

l: Dharmraj, Asa ki War (Asa di Var), Slok II .. Pauri II
s: Dharmraj is appointed by God to judge and record the acts of animals.

l: divine order, Asa ki War (Asa di Var), Slok II .. Pauri II
s: God's order determines whom He absorbs, destroys, withdraws from mammon, or causes to remain therein.

l: God's court, Asa ki War (Asa di Var), Slok II .. Pauri II
s: God's court is described as true. At His own court, the real truth is adjudged, and those attached to mammon are separated and removed.

l: meditation on the True One, Asa ki War (Asa di Var), Slok II .. Pauri II
s: Those who meditate on the True One are declared true by Guru Nanak.

l: birth and death, Asa ki War (Asa di Var), Slok II .. Pauri II
s: Those who are born and die are described by Guru Nanak as the falsest of the false.

l: divine glory, Asa ki War (Asa di Var), Slok II .. Pauri II
s: God's glory is called great because His name is great, His justice is true, His seat is immovable, He understands utterances, knows feelings, gives without consulting others, and is all in all Himself. His acts cannot be described.

l: divine will, Asa ki War (Asa di Var), Slok II .. Pauri II
s: All that God did and has to do depends on His own will.

l: God's court, Asa ki War (Asa di Var), Slok II .. Pauri II
s: Guru Angad describes this world as the True One's chamber, with the True One's dwelling therein.

l: mammon, Asa ki War (Asa di Var), Slok II .. Pauri II
s: God withdraws some from mammon and causes others to abide therein. Those attached to mammon are separated and removed from the divine court.

l: holiness, Asa ki War (Asa di Var), Slok II .. Pauri II
s: The person to whom God reveals Himself is known as holy.

l: animals, Asa ki War (Asa di Var), Slok II .. Pauri II
s: God created animals, recorded their names, and appointed Dharmraj to judge their acts.

l: names, Asa ki War (Asa di Var), Slok II .. Pauri II
s: God recorded the names of the animals He created.

l: judgment of acts, Asa ki War (Asa di Var), Slok II .. Pauri II
s: God appointed Dharmraj to judge and record acts. At God's court, the real truth is adjudged.

l: hell, Asa ki War (Asa di Var), Slok II .. Pauri II
s: The false find no place at God's court and go to hell with blackened faces.

l: Asa ki War (Asa di Var), Asa ki War (Asa di Var), Slok III .. Pauri III
s: Guru Nanak describes the wonder of God's word, knowledge, creatures, natural elements, human experiences, and the meeting and parting from God. He teaches that all things, including creation, virtues, vices, honour, dishonour, and religious compositions, exist by God's power. Pauri III explains that man eventually becomes ashes, while the soul passes away and ministers of Death take the dead for judgment. The Judge reads an account of his acts and passes sentence, leaving the condemned without shelter.

l: Guru Nanak, Asa ki War (Asa di Var), Slok III .. Pauri III
s: Guru Nanak marvels at the wonders of God's works and says that those who understand them are supremely fortunate. He teaches that everything exists by God's power and that God is unrivalled.

l: animals, Asa ki War (Asa di Var), Slok III .. Pauri III
s: Creatures have wonderful species, forms, colours, genera, and kinds. Their existence and characteristics arise by God's power.

l: divine power, Asa ki War (Asa di Var), Slok III .. Pauri III
s: Power is attributed to God and is the cause of seeing, hearing, fear, happiness, creation, affection, virtues, vices, honour, dishonour, and the elements. Everything exists by this power.

l: creation, Asa ki War (Asa di Var), Slok III .. Pauri III
s: Creation exists by God's power, including the nether regions, the heavens, the earth, and all creatures. God pervades and commands all creation.

l: men, Asa ki War (Asa di Var), Slok III .. Pauri III
s: Man enjoys himself but eventually becomes ashes. However wealthy or great he is, ministers of Death take him away, and a judgment of his acts follows; the condemned finds no shelter and no one hears his cries.

l: soul, Asa ki War (Asa di Var), Slok III .. Pauri III
s: The soul passes away after man becomes ashes.

l: Death, Asa ki War (Asa di Var), Slok III .. Pauri III
s: Death takes man away after his life, regardless of his greatness or wealth.

l: ministers of Death, Asa ki War (Asa di Var), Slok III .. Pauri III
s: The ministers of Death throw a chain around a man's neck and take him away for judgment.

l: account of his acts, Asa ki War (Asa di Var), Slok III .. Pauri III
s: An account of the man's acts is read before the Judge. The account is used in passing sentence.

l: Judge, Asa ki War (Asa di Var), Slok III .. Pauri III
s: The Judge sits on a seat, reads the account of the man's acts, and passes sentence.

l: life, Asa ki War (Asa di Var), Slok III .. Pauri III
s: Man can waste his life while blind to his condition. Afterward, he becomes ashes and faces judgment.

l: Asa ki War (Asa di Var), Asa ki War (Asa di Var), Slok IV .. Pauri IV
s: Guru Nanak describes fear as governing winds, rivers, fire, earth, Indar, Dharmraj, the sun, the moon, spiritual beings, stars, heroes, and the movements of people, while God, the Formless One, alone is without fear. He teaches that worldly rulers, performers, ornaments, bodies, and religious compositions do not provide divine knowledge. Divine knowledge is obtained by God's grace rather than by words, skill, or orders. The Pauri says that the true Guru is obtained through the Kind One's kindness, gives the Word to the wandering soul, removes pride, and leads people to the True One.

l: Guru Nanak, Asa ki War (Asa di Var), Slok IV .. Pauri IV
s: Guru Nanak teaches that God, the Formless One, alone is without fear, and that all other beings and movements occur in fear. He also says that divine knowledge is not gained through mere words, skill, or orders.

l: God, Asa ki War (Asa di Var), Slok IV .. Pauri IV
s: God has destined fear for every one, while the Formless One and the True is alone without fear. By God's grace, a person obtains divine knowledge.

l: True Guru, Asa ki War (Asa di Var), Slok IV .. Pauri IV
s: The true Guru is obtained when the Kind One looks with kindness. The true Guru communicates the Word to the soul, removes pride from his heart, preaches the Truest of the true, and leads people to obtain the True One.

l: fear, Asa ki War (Asa di Var), Slok IV .. Pauri IV
s: Fear governs the winds, rivers, fire, earth, Indar, Dharmraj, the sun, the moon, spiritual beings, stars, firmament, mighty men, divine heroes, and the coming and going of people. The Formless One alone is without fear.

l: divine knowledge, Asa ki War (Asa di Var), Slok IV .. Pauri IV
s: Divine knowledge is not sought in mere words, and speaking about it is difficult. A person obtains it by God's grace, not through skill or orders.

l: Word, Asa ki War (Asa di Var), Slok IV .. Pauri IV
s: The true Guru communicates the Word to the soul after it has wandered through many births.

l: God's grace, Asa ki War (Asa di Var), Slok IV .. Pauri IV
s: God's grace enables a person to obtain divine knowledge.

l: Asa ki War (Asa di Var), Asa ki War (Asa di Var), Slok V .. Pauri V
s: Guru Nanak describes worldly performers, objects, and beings as caught in entanglements and turned according to their own acts. He teaches that those without divine knowledge are consumed by the minister of death, while the Formless One creates the whole world and shows kindness to favored worshippers. Guru's instruction gives knowledge and saves those upon whom the Kind One looks with favor. The name, good acts, humility, fear of God, and love are presented as beneficial, while death comes when a person's measure is full.

l: Guru Nanak, Asa ki War (Asa di Var), Slok V .. Pauri V
s: Guru Nanak describes the world as a stage of performers and turning objects, and teaches that beings dance according to their own acts. He also teaches that those with fear of God have love and that death comes when a person's measure is full.

l: God, Asa ki War (Asa di Var), Slok V .. Pauri V
s: The Formless One is fearless, has a true name, and has the whole world as its creation. Repeating the name of the Formless One keeps a person from hell.

l: divine knowledge, Asa ki War (Asa di Var), Slok V .. Pauri V
s: Those who are devoid of divine knowledge are robbed and consumed by the minister of death.

l: ministers of Death, Asa ki War (Asa di Var), Slok V .. Pauri V
s: The minister of death devours those who are devoid of divine knowledge.

l: world, Asa ki War (Asa di Var), Slok V .. Pauri V
s: The whole world is described as the creation of the Formless One and as a stage with properties and vessels that are entanglements.

l: Guru's instruction, Asa ki War (Asa di Var), Slok V .. Pauri V
s: Through the Guru's instruction, disciples obtain knowledge that the Kind One saves those upon whom He looks with favor.

l: the Kind One, Asa ki War (Asa di Var), Slok V .. Pauri V
s: The Kind One saves those upon whom He looks with favor.

l: entanglements of the world, Asa ki War (Asa di Var), Slok V .. Pauri V
s: Entanglements include the stage properties and vessels of the world, and those bound in them are swung round. Everyone dances according to their own acts, and those who dance and laugh shall weep when they depart.

l: fear of God, Asa ki War (Asa di Var), Slok V .. Pauri V
s: Those who have the fear of God in their hearts also have love.

l: love, Asa ki War (Asa di Var), Slok V .. Pauri V
s: Love is found in those who have the fear of God in their hearts.

l: the true Name, Asa ki War (Asa di Var), Slok V .. Pauri V
s: Repeating the name keeps a person from going to hell. The name is identified with the Formless One.

l: good deeds, Asa ki War (Asa di Var), Slok V .. Pauri V
s: A person seeking advantage is instructed to do good acts and be lowly.

l: death, Asa ki War (Asa di Var), Slok V .. Pauri V
s: Death comes even if a person manages to stave off old age. None may remain when his measure is full.

l: Asa ki War (Asa di Var), Asa ki War (Asa di Var), Slok VI .. Pauri VI
s: The unit contrasts the religious practices of Musalmans, Hindus, and Jogis with the service of God and the conduct of generous, sinful, and worldly people. It teaches that saints hunger to praise God and rely on the true Name, abiding in everlasting joy. Guru Nanak reflects on the fate of a Musalman's ashes and leaves the matter to the Creator. Pauri VI teaches that none finds God without the true Guru, through whom salvation is obtained.

l: Musalmans, Asa ki War (Asa di Var), Slok VI .. Pauri VI
s: Musalmans praise and study the Shariat, but God's servants employ themselves in His service to behold Him. Their ashes may be made into vessels and bricks, where they burn, weep, and send forth sparks.

l: Hindus, Asa ki War (Asa di Var), Slok VI .. Pauri VI
s: Hindus praise the Praised One, bathe in holy streams, perform idol-worship and adoration, and use copious sandal incense.

l: God, Asa ki War (Asa di Var), Slok VI .. Pauri VI
s: God is the One whom His servants seek to behold. He cares for all animals, beings, and creation, and the true Guru manifests and proclaims that God has put Himself into him.

l: Jogis, Asa ki War (Asa di Var), Slok VI .. Pauri VI
s: Jogis meditate on God the Creator, whom they call the Unseen, the Bright One, and the image of their bodies.

l: saints, Asa ki War (Asa di Var), Slok VI .. Pauri VI
s: Saints hunger to praise God and abide in everlasting joy day and night. The text asks to obtain the dust of the feet of such virtuous men.

l: the true Name, Asa ki War (Asa di Var), Slok VI .. Pauri VI
s: The true Name supports the saints as they praise God, and they abide in everlasting joy through it.

l: Guru Nanak, Asa ki War (Asa di Var), Slok VI .. Pauri VI
s: Guru Nanak states that the Creator knows whether it is better for a Musalman's ashes to be burned or buried.

l: True Guru, Asa ki War (Asa di Var), Slok VI .. Pauri VI
s: Without the true Guru none has found God. The true Guru has God within him, banishes worldly love, and leads to salvation through meeting him.

l: salvation, Asa ki War (Asa di Var), Slok VI .. Pauri VI
s: Salvation is ever obtained by meeting the true Guru, who has banished worldly love from within him.

l: Asa ki War (Asa di Var), Asa ki War (Asa di Var), Slok VII .. Pauri VII
s: The unit concerns man, pride, God, Nanak, transmigration, and people who have meditated on God. It teaches that pride affects nearly every aspect of man's life and conduct, and that when pride is removed, God's gate is seen. Pride subjects man to repeated transmigration, but God's grace and the Guru's instruction provide a medicine for it. People who have meditated on God as the truest of the true have worshipped, lived honestly, rejected evil, and found Him.

l: men, Asa ki War (Asa di Var), Slok VII .. Pauri VII
s: Man is born, dies, gives, takes, earns, spends, rejoices, mourns, and becomes true or false in pride. Man may go to hell or heaven according to pride, but when pride is removed, God's gate is seen. Without divine knowledge, man troubles himself by talking, and as he regards God, God regards him.

l: pride, Asa ki War (Asa di Var), Slok VII .. Pauri VII
s: Pride affects man's birth, death, actions, thoughts, status, knowledge, wealth, and spiritual condition. Pride is a chronic disease and a trammel that subjects man to repeated transmigration, but it departs through God's grace and the Guru's instruction.

l: God, Asa ki War (Asa di Var), Slok VII .. Pauri VII
s: God's gate is seen when pride is removed. God may bestow grace, through which man can receive the Guru's instruction, and God gives gifts that increase a quarterfold.

l: Guru Nanak, Asa ki War (Asa di Var), Slok VII .. Pauri VII
s: Nanak states that the Commander has ordained that as man regards God, so God regards him. Nanak also teaches that through God's grace and the Guru's instruction, trouble caused by pride shall depart.

l: transmigration, Asa ki War (Asa di Var), Slok VII .. Pauri VII
s: Transmigration is repeated wandering to which pride subjects man. Man wanders according to his previous acts.

l: people who have meditated on God, Asa ki War (Asa di Var), Slok VII .. Pauri VII
s: People who have meditated on God as the truest of the true have performed real worship and become contented. They have refrained from evil, done good deeds, practised honesty, lived on little corn and water, broken the entanglements of the world, and found God.

l: Asa ki War (Asa di Var), Asa ki War (Asa di Var), Slok VIII .. Pauri VIII
s: The unit concerns God’s creation and care of the world, including men, trees, animals, lands, waters, and the universe. It teaches that God creates animals and takes care of them, and that the Creator who made the world also takes thought for it. Guru Nanak says that good deeds, charities, penances, bravery, study, and reading sacred works are of no avail without the mark of grace, while God has decreed transmigration. The passage teaches that truth comes from God and is obtained by meeting the true Guru, but the fool wastes life through obstinacy.

l: Guru Nanak, Asa ki War (Asa di Var), Slok VIII .. Pauri VIII
s: Guru Nanak teaches that hundreds of thousands of good deeds, charities, penances, acts of bravery, studies, and readings would be of no avail without the true mark of grace. He states that the Creator who made the world has decreed transmigration.

l: God, Asa ki War (Asa di Var), Slok VIII .. Pauri VIII
s: God creates men, trees, animals, lands, waters, the universe, and the sources of production, and He knows their condition. God takes care of all animals, and the Creator who made the world also takes thought for it. His court is imperishable.

l: animals, Asa ki War (Asa di Var), Slok VIII .. Pauri VIII
s: Animals are among the beings created by God. God takes care of them all and knows their condition.

l: world, Asa ki War (Asa di Var), Slok VIII .. Pauri VIII
s: The world is created by God, who also takes thought for it. The Creator who made the world has decreed transmigration.

l: the true Name, Asa ki War (Asa di Var), Slok VIII .. Pauri VIII
s: The true Name is necessary for a sacrificial mark or sacrificial thread to have value.

l: grace, Asa ki War (Asa di Var), Slok VIII .. Pauri VIII
s: Grace provides the true mark. Without the mark of grace, numerous good acts, charities, penances, acts of bravery, studies, and readings are of no avail.

l: transmigration, Asa ki War (Asa di Var), Slok VIII .. Pauri VIII
s: Transmigration is decreed by the Creator who made the world.

l: truth, Asa ki War (Asa di Var), Slok VIII .. Pauri VIII
s: Truth is diffused by the true Lord. A person receives truth from the Lord and practises it after meeting the true Guru in whose heart truth dwells.

l: True Guru, Asa ki War (Asa di Var), Slok VIII .. Pauri VIII
s: The true Guru is one in whose heart truth dwells. A person obtains truth by meeting the true Guru.

l: Asa ki War (Asa di Var), Asa ki War (Asa di Var), Slok IX .. Pauri IX
s: This unit concerns Guru Nanak’s teachings on books, religious practices, actions, and devotion to God. It says that reading, pilgrimage, religious garb, austerity, silence, wilderness dwelling, and other outward practices are useless without God's name and guidance from a guru. Man suffers through attachment to mammon and must bear the results of his own acts, while those who meet the true Guru and fix God's name in their hearts obtain comfort and freedom from hopes, fears, and pride. The saints please God and gain entrance to His gate, while distinctions of caste are contrasted with the speaker’s low-caste identity and meditation on God.

l: Guru Nanak, Asa ki War (Asa di Var), Slok IX .. Pauri IX
s: Guru Nanak teaches that only God's name has lasting account, while excessive reading and outward religious practices become senseless or harmful without devotion. He also teaches that meeting the true Guru and fixing God's name in the heart brings comfort and destroys pride.

l: God, Asa ki War (Asa di Var), Slok IX .. Pauri IX
s: God is the object of true remembrance and devotion. God looks with favour on some, grants them Himself, and is pleased by the saints, while those outside His favour find no entrance and wander through many births.

l: men, Asa ki War (Asa di Var), Slok IX .. Pauri IX
s: Man may read books for his whole life, wander on pilgrimages, wear religious garbs, avoid corn or clothes, remain silent, sleep in ignorance, go barefoot, eat filth, or dwell in wilderness and burial and cremation-grounds, yet he still suffers for his own acts. Man obtains comfort only by meeting the true Guru and fixing God's name in his heart.

l: books, Asa ki War (Asa di Var), Slok IX .. Pauri IX
s: Books may be loaded into carts and boats, used to fill pits, and read for months, years, or a lifetime. The text says that such reading is of no account compared with one word, God's name.

l: God's name, Asa ki War (Asa di Var), Slok IX .. Pauri IX
s: God's name is presented as the only word that truly counts. Fixing it in the heart brings comfort, freedom from hopes and fears, and an abiding place.

l: account of his acts, Asa ki War (Asa di Var), Slok IX .. Pauri IX
s: Man must bear the results of his own acts. Outward austerities and unusual practices do not remove the suffering caused by those acts.

l: True Guru, Asa ki War (Asa di Var), Slok IX .. Pauri IX
s: A guru is necessary to awaken one who sleeps in ignorance. The true Guru gives comfort when man meets him and fixes God's name in his heart.
